The best medication i've found for minor or moderate pain has been Paracetamol and Ibuprofen which can be used together. Paracetamol will be 1000mg dose(anymore than 1000mg doesn't have any added effect on the pain) and the Ibuprofen a 400mg dose (with the Ibuprofen you can go safely to a 800mg dose)

When we get into the world of teeth and jaw infections the pain is typically moderate to severe and Paracetamol/Ibuprofen do very little for the pain. With this level of pain you'll have to move into the world of Opiates.

For most people a dose of 60mg of Codeine and a 1000mg of Paracetamol will do the trick for pain relief, again also taking Ibuprofen will help with the inflammation. (note people metabolize Codeine differently, some will get no benefit from it whatsoever and you'll have to use an alternative pain reliever like Tramadol)

The antibiotic Amoxicillin is what you need to treat a tooth abscess. You take one 500mg tablet at breakfast, lunch and dinner for a week, a total of 20 tablets.

If you end up with other periodontal problems like gum disease or if the infection spreads to the bone you'll need an antibiotic called Metronidazole. Metronidazole is taken in 400mg dose's, one tablet at breakfast, lunch and dinner for a week, a total of 21 tablets. (Both Amoxicillin and Metronidazole can be taken at the same time)
